source.citation: Blakely, R.J., Langenheim, V.E., Ponce, D.A., and Dixon, G.L. (2000), Aeromagnetic Survey of the Amargosa Desert, Nevada and California: A Tool for Understanding Near-Surface Geology and Hydrology, USGS Open-File Report 00-188, doi:10.3133/ofr2000188.
source.processing_state: USGS provider-processed levelled total-field anomaly; original corrections retained, none reapplied here
source.sensor_height_reference: radar height above terrain as reported by USGS

configuration.sensor_height_reference: radar height above terrain as reported by USGS

exact_collocation_qc.interpretation: exactly coincident mapped samples only; no near-crossing interpolation

crossover_interpolation_qc.interpretation: segment-linear crossover QC only; no leveling or correction applied

split.unit: contiguous interior block of entire flight lines
split.line_order_by: survey-center projection onto estimated flight-line normal

heldout_interpolation.interpretation: spatial interpolation on withheld whole flight lines; not a subsurface inverse

limitations: No source correction or tie-line levelling was performed.
Grid values outside the training convex hull are masked as unsupported.
Tie-line observations are retained for geometry/height QC and are not used to fit the grid.
A provider grid comparison is unavailable until the matching source product is acquired.
Held-out interpolation accuracy is not subsurface-model accuracy.

source_selection.sensor_height: radar height, metres above terrain per source report
limitations: USGS provider processing already removed diurnal and IGRF fields and applied navigation and crossover levelling.
The provider-levelled channel is used as published; no provider corrections are repeated.
One longest source segment represents each cross-track cluster; omitted segment IDs remain listed.
The ROI interpolation and blocked-line score are local processing diagnostics, not subsurface recovery or independent-site validation.
